description: Juniper EX4400-48F campus access switch with fibre ports, 1RU. It has 36 SFP ports for 100 Mbps or 1GbE optics. It has 12 SFP/SFP+ ports for 1GbE or 10GbE optics. They sit in 24 columns of two cages. The front also holds a USB-C console port, the chassis and port mode lamps, a mode button and one extension module slot. The rear holds two 100GbE QSFP28 ports, console, management and USB-A ports, two fan modules and two power supply slots. A shipped switch carries one 550 W supply, two fan modules and covers on the empty slots. The configurations give the supply type and the airflow, and the -S spare ships with no supply and no fans.

gaps.note: Table 18 prints "100/1000/2500/5000/10000BASE-X ports: 12" for the 48F, the speed list of the multigigabit copper models. The note under it, Table 44, Table 114 and the opening of the 48F topic all give these 12 ports as SFP+ ports for 1G and 10G optics. The SFP+ speeds are modelled and the printed row is not used.

The -S spare takes a 550 W VDC supply, JPSU-550-C-VDC-AFO (Figure 86, Tables 74 and 77, 24 cm deep), which the library has no part for. The -S configuration leaves both supply bays open and the bays do not accept the VDC supply, so it is not offered. The 550 W AC and DC supplies of the other builds are seated as in the 24T.

name: ex4400-48f

airflow.note: Tables 17 and 19 - the 48F is sold front-to-back (AIR OUT label, orange handle) as EX4400-48F and EX4400-48F-DC, and back-to-front (AIR IN label, blue handle) as EX4400-48F-AFI and EX4400-48F-DC-AFI. The -S spare ships with no supply and no fan modules, and the guide says a buyer orders them separately, front-to-back or back-to-front.

colour.note: Median of bare face on the guide renders (#777777 at the front, #707070 at the rear) and of the status plate (#50575f). The 24X studio photograph shows the same mid-grey finish. The legends of the non-PoE models are near white on the render.

extension-slot.note: Figure 22 callout 7. The slot is a recess 363.8 to 437.8 across and 17.7 to 41.2 down in the render of Figure 19, which draws a four-cage module seated; a shipped switch has the cover, because the shipped-components statement under Table 18 names one cover for the empty extension module slot. The slot is a bay and takes the three extension modules the guide names.

gate-1.note: Figure 19 (g022661, 1500 x 199 px, embedded image extracted from the PDF) gives a face 1297 px wide (83 to 1379.5) and about 127 px tall, which is 2.936 px per mm across on the stated 441.7 mm and 2.92 down on 43.7 mm. The SFP cage width on that scale reads 13.96 mm and the column pitch 14.2 mm, the registry's 14.25 ganged pitch, measured on a quantity the scale never saw. The rear render (Figure 20, g022646, 2000 x 265 px) gives a face 1733.5 px by 168.5 px, aspect 10.29, 3.92 px per mm across and 3.86 down. Positions are taken per axis on those scales and each reads to about half a millimetre on the front and a quarter on the rear.

grounding.note: Connect Earth Ground to an EX4400 Switch - a 2-hole protective grounding terminal on the rear panel, used with 10-32 x 0.25 in screws and the lugs LCD10-10AF-L, LCD8-10AF-L or LCD6-10AF-L. The guide gives no hole spacing. The 15.0 mm spacing is measured on the render and is estimated. The render shows two bare holes, so they are drawn as dark holes on the plate.

interface-names.note: Table 114 - the CLI addresses the switch as FPC 0, the built-in ports as PIC 0 ports 0 to 47, the two rear QSFP28 ports as PIC 1 ports 0 and 1, and the extension module as PIC 2. The names are not printed on the metal, so no interfaces block is written.

mounting.note: Mounting Options and the mounting procedures - the two-post kit EX-RMK ships in the box and mounts the brackets flush with the front or along the middle of the side panels. The separately orderable EX-4PST-RMK mounts the switch flush with the front posts of a four-post rack or recessed inside it. EX-WMK is a wall kit. No ear distance in millimetres, no rack depth range and no bracket drawing that can be measured is in the guide, so the positions are named without a number and no kit is listed. The library holds no rail kit for them.

port-leds.note: Figures 52 and 53 (g022609 and its SFP+ twin) and Tables 43 and 44 - each port has a link activity lamp and a status lamp, four small triangles in the belly between the two cages. From the left they are the lower port's link lamp, the upper port's link lamp, the lower port's status lamp and the upper port's status lamp (callouts 4, 1, 3 and 2). The upper port's triangles point up and the lower port's down. They sit 2.6, 5.3, 8.95 and 11.65 mm from the column's left edge, 11.0 mm below the top of the upper cage, read off the render of the 24X face, which has the same cage and lamp artwork, and estimated. The link lamp is green, steady for a link without traffic and blinking for traffic. The status lamp shows one parameter at a time, chosen with the mode button.

port-numbering.note: Figure 19 and Figure 22 - under each column one pair, an even number with an up arrow and the next odd number with a down arrow ("0 up 1 down" to "46 up 47 down"). Numbering starts at 0, as printed. The legend sits 28.1 mm below the upper cage's top, the arrows 5.9 and 11.0 mm from the column's left edge; both are estimated from the render. CLI names are not printed on the metal and Table 114 gives the ports as PIC 0 ports 0 to 47.

port-speeds.note: Table 18 and its notes - with fibre transceivers, ports 0 to 35 run 100 Mbps and 1000 Mbps and ports 36 to 47 run 1000 Mbps and 10 Gbps. With a 1G SFP-T transceiver, ports 0 to 35 run 10, 100 and 1000 Mbps and ports 36 to 47 run 1000 Mbps. The EX-SFP-1FE-FX, -SX and -LX optics do not autonegotiate on ports 36 to 47. Table 44 gives the SPD lamp - 1000 Mbps steady and 100 Mbps blinking on the SFP ports, 10 Gbps steady and 1000 Mbps blinking on the SFP+ ports.

ports.note: Figure 19 and Figure 22 - 48 SFP-family ports in two rows of 24, in four blocks of six columns on the registry's 14.25 mm ganged pitch with a 3.35 mm gutter, so the block step is 88.85 mm (6.13, 95.03, 183.92 and 272.48 mm at the first cage of each block on the render). The first cage opens at 5.9 mm. The upper cage starts 9.9 mm down and the lower 14.9 mm below it. The first 36 ports (three blocks) are SFP and the last 12 (the fourth block) are SFP+, so the face is two port groups and two blocks. Counts confirmed by Table 18 (10/100/1000BASE-X ports 36 and 100/1000/2500/5000/10000BASE-X ports 12 - the row is misprinted, see the gap built-in-port-row) and Table 114 (PIC 0, 36x1G SFP and 12x1G/10G SFP/SFP+).

power-supplies.note: Table 17 ships the 48F with a 550 W AC supply, and Table 19 gives the same for the other builds. The text under Figure 22 says the 48F takes 550 W AC or DC supplies and that the -S spare takes the 550 W VDC supply, and that AC, DC and VDC must not be mixed. The rear renders show two supplies; the default here ships one supply and a cover on the second slot, as the text under Table 18 states. A bay cannot say that supplies of one chassis must match.

rear.note: Figure 20 and Figure 23 measured on the render, per axis, from the rear left edge (the chassis right side as seen from the front). CON jack centre 18.35, 13.6; MGMT jack centre 39.6, 13.6, both with the contact comb up; USB-A at 55.0, 12.5, vertical; RESET pinhole at 55.3, 24.9; ground plate 27.8 to 61.7 across and 27.6 to 39.7 down with two threaded holes 15.0 apart at 39.5 and 54.5; QSFP28 cages centred at 75.5 across and 14.5 and 28.2 down, labelled 0 and 1 to their left; two columns of lamps at 89.4 and 94.3 across, two for each cage per row; ESD socket at 101.1, 36.0. Fan module slots are at 108.2 and 206.0 across, and power supply slots at 255.0 and 346.4 across, each with a fan or power icon and its number above the slot or beside it. All of these are estimated from the render, to about 0.3 mm. The guide draws one rear for the 24T, 24P, 48T, 48P, 48F, 24MP and 48MP, and the callout list of Figure 23 is the same as that of the other models.

rear-labels.note: Figure 23 callouts 1, 6, 10 and 15 are the serial number ID label, the CLEI code label, the power supply rating label and the claim code label. They are stickers, not metal, so each is a named region and is not drawn. The render shows them as blank plates. The guide shows no content, and none is invented.

sources.note: EX4400 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, PDF created 2026-07-22 (331 pages), fetched from www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4400/ex4400.pdf. Taken from it - Table 4 and Table 7 (the model list), Tables 17 to 19 with Figures 19 to 24 (EX4400-48F), Table 5 (extension modules), Table 38 to Table 40 (chassis, fan and supply sizes), Tables 41 to 51 (lamps), Tables 52 to 58 and Tables 73 to 80 (heat and supplies), Table 93 (environment), Table 105 (what ships), Table 114 (CLI names) and Table 115 (acoustics). Figures 19 and 20 (g022661, g022646) are renders of the real product and are the pictures measured here; Figure 21 (g022649) is the DC rear. Juniper's image library answered for none of the 48F views - the address ex4400-48f/ex4400-48f-front-high.jpg returned an HTML 404 page, as did the 24MP and 48MP - so the guide's renders are the only picture of each face. The 24X studio photograph, which shares the chassis and the status block, confirms the colour and finish. The EX4400 datasheet on juniper.net (a French-language PDF of 2025-10-14, the only one the site answers for) lists the 48F as 12 SFP+ 10GbE and 36 SFP 1GbE ports; no figure here comes from it. Terms - Juniper's documentation pages state no licence for the guide, so the facts are transcribed and nothing is copied; no drawing or photograph is in the repository. The held intake folder was not readable by this account, so no earlier photograph, stencil or 3D model could be used. An end-of-life search made 2026-10-20 found no notice for the EX4400 line, so the lifecycle is none-announced.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) - a belly-to-belly pair is the upper cage upright and the lower turned 180. The render shows the latch bars in the belly between the cages, which agrees. The rear QSFP28 cages are stacked this way too, and the render at 3.9 px per mm does not resolve which way their latches point, so the rule decides and a photograph overturns it.

status-block.note: Figure 22 callouts 3 to 6 and Figure 19. A dark plate 361.2 to 439.5 across and 1.4 to 15.5 down. The model name EX4400-48F is printed at the left from 367.7 mm. The USB-C console port is centred at 393.7, 8.3 with the USB symbol below it. Two columns of lamps sit at 406.2 and 410.1 across - SYS, ALM, MST and CLD on the left, SPD, DX and EN on the right, with no POE lamp on a non-PoE model. The rows are at 3.8, 6.8, 9.7 and 12.8 down; the render scatters them by up to 0.5 mm and they are aligned. The mode button is a flush disc at 423.1, 8.6.

vents.note: The front has a hexagon punching in a band over and under the port blocks, from the logo to the status block. The rear punching is two small fields above and below the QSFP28 cages. The fields are drawn as a repeating pattern in simplified outlines, not hole for hole.

width.note: Table 18 gives the chassis 17.39 in (44.17 cm) wide, and says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in (48.2 cm). The face is the body between the folds, 441.7 mm, with no ears drawn. Height is 1.72 in (4.37 cm), 1RU. Depth is 15.71 in (39.9 cm) with no supply, fan module or extension module fitted, 16.93 in (43 cm) with a supply and fan modules, 17.35 in (44.07 cm) with an extension module as well. The bare figure 399.0 mm is carried as the chassis depth, because every module is its own part. The other two are in attrs.
